text:
The judge should instruct the jury that self-defense requires a reasonable belief in imminent unlawful force, and the father’s mistaken belief must be judged by whether a reasonable person in his circumstances would have believed deadly force was necessary. Because the son had repeatedly abused him and was kicking down the door after being locked out, the jury may consider the father’s history and fear in assessing reasonableness, but if the son did not actually intend harm and the father’s belief was unreasonable, self-defense would fail. The instruction should therefore submit the reasonableness of the father’s belief to the jury rather than rule on it as a matter of law.  
CONFIDENCE: 82
